correctness.rationale: The classical exact facet description for K5-minor-free cut polytopes was checked against its primary PDF (Barahona–Mahjoub, Cor. 3.10). Cut-vector linear identities ensure full dimension, switchings force an optimal half-edge center, and the facet-dilation equality is proved by testing reflected containment. Every cycle restriction has even parity; exact opposite support computation yields quotient 1 on even cycles and length/(length−2) on odd cycles. Shortest odd cycles are chordless and maximize the decreasing quotient. No unproven numerical step enters the universal proof. The packaged exact-rational verifier corroborated 1,288 small graphs, 23,906 inequalities and 1,867,540 reflected inequalities.

originality.rationale: An exact statement/implication comparison of genuinely inspected primary full texts finds facet classifications and switching geometry, or one-skeleton graph distances, but not this optimized reflection scaling by shortest odd cycle. Barahona–Mahjoub provides a crucial stronger input for facet description, not the claimed asymmetry conclusion. Index and targeted web searches found no equivalent formula. Residual nomenclature and priority risk remains; failure to find coverage is not taken as proof of global novelty.
residual_risks: An earlier publication could state the equivalent measure under symmetry ratio, critical-center scaling, parity-polytope nomenclature or a graph-theoretic reformulation.
The facet theorem is classical and the new observation is the exact symmetry optimization; its perceived novelty may differ from bibliographic priority.
A highly relevant otherwise inaccessible book treatment may contain an unstated equivalent formula; no such positive coverage was identified.

value.rationale: Minkowski asymmetry is a classical intrinsic affine-invariant statistic. The result computes it exactly for every nontrivial K5-minor-free cut polytope and shows a structural odd-girth law independent of graph order, bridges, and other cycles. It yields a complete bipartite/central-symmetry boundary and sharp quantitative behavior along high odd-girth families. This is a motivated exact classification, not a numerical certificate or arbitrary specialized slice.
